# CPDataKit v0.11.0

The CSV workbench can now save confirmed import settings and load them for the next file.
Matching files reuse output names, types, units, roles and excluded columns. A changed column
order, name, visible unit, detected type or parsing option produces a before/after preview;
the workbench does not automatically apply the old declarations to that file.

Settings reuse the existing parsing and column contracts. They exclude source hashes, data values
and experiment descriptions. Each import still requires fresh source information and confirmation,
and records its own hash and settings comparison. Legacy settings without a source signature
can restore parsing options but require fresh field declarations.

Real echemdb and PyIRoGlass cases verify numeric values, units, order and independent provenance.
Within the workbench, the second curve avoids re-entering six unit cells and three roles;
the second spectrum avoids two names, four unit cells and two roles. These are declaration counts,
not measured time savings or a demonstrated net advantage over the native projects.

Headerless or indistinguishable columns and units absent from CSV still require source review.
PyIRoGlass testing uses its unchanged reader source because the full package could not be installed
in the tested Windows environment. No MCMC, scientific inference or experimental validation is added.

Python remains >=3.12. Runtime dependencies, existing data formats and release workflows are unchanged.
See the [workbench guide](https://github.com/koocmitwho/cpdatakit/blob/v0.11.0/docs/workbench-guide.md),
[real-data cases](https://github.com/koocmitwho/cpdatakit/blob/v0.11.0/examples/repeated-import/README.md)
and [verification record](https://github.com/koocmitwho/cpdatakit/blob/v0.11.0/docs/verification/2026-10-07-v0110.md).
